attachments.origin_landmark: long head: ischial tuberosity, inferomedial facet of the upper area (with semitendinosus, via conjoint tendon); short head: linea aspera of femur (femur_r)

functional_compartments.name: Long head
functional_compartments.function_note: Crosses both hip and knee; extends hip in addition to flexing knee.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset; Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_from: the superior medial aspect of the ischial tuberosity
motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_to: the proximal aspect of the medial femoral epicondyle
motor_endplate_zones.method: cadaveric dissection to the proximal and distal limit points of the terminal intramuscular nerve endings
motor_endplate_zones.notes: The long head's arborisation, measured on a line that runs PROXIMAL to DISTAL -- the opposite direction to the hamstring line used by Rha and by the entries on semitendinosus and semimembranosus, so the two are not directly comparable without inverting one. The motor entry point itself, where the branch first pierces the belly, is at 41.5% on this line (and 36.3% on the source's perpendicular axis from the tuberosity toward the greater trochanter), near the proximal limit of the arborised field.
motor_endplate_zones.source: An XC, Lee JH, Im S, Lee MS, Hwang K, Kim HW, Han SH, 'Anatomic localization of motor entry points and intramuscular nerve endings in the hamstring muscles', Surg Radiol Anat 32(6):529-537 (2010), doi:10.1007/s00276-009-0609-5 -- 50 cadaveric lower extremities. Retrieved via PubMed.

motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_from: the medial and lateral TIBIAL condyles
motor_endplate_zones.method: modified Sihler stain intramuscular arborisation mapping
motor_endplate_zones.notes: Proximal of the two bands this source reports for biceps femoris as a whole; it does not separate the heads. On this DISTAL-to-PROXIMAL line, 50-60% is 40-50% of the way down from the tuberosity, which falls inside the long head's arborised field as measured independently by An et al. (39.7-72.9% from the tuberosity). Two studies, opposite reference directions, agreeing.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Rha DW, Yi KH, Park ES, Park C, Kim HJ, 'Intramuscular nerve distribution of the hamstring muscles: Application to treating spasticity', Clin Anat 29(6):746-751 (2016), doi:10.1002/ca.22735 -- 10 specimens per muscle, modified Sihler method. Retrieved via PubMed.

motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_from: the medial and lateral TIBIAL condyles
motor_endplate_zones.method: modified Sihler stain intramuscular arborisation mapping
motor_endplate_zones.notes: Distal of the two bands, equivalent to 70-85% of the way down from the ischial tuberosity. It lies in the distal third of the thigh, where the two heads are fused and a needle cannot be assigned to one head by position alone -- An et al. put the short head's field at 58.9-80.2% and the long head's at 39.7-72.9% from the tuberosity, which overlap here.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Rha DW, Yi KH, Park ES, Park C, Kim HJ, 'Intramuscular nerve distribution of the hamstring muscles: Application to treating spasticity', Clin Anat 29(6):746-751 (2016), doi:10.1002/ca.22735 -- 10 specimens per muscle, modified Sihler method. Retrieved via PubMed.

functional_compartments.name: Short head
functional_compartments.innervation_branch: common fibular (peroneal) division of sciatic n.
functional_compartments.function_note: Crosses only the knee; textbook example of a single named muscle with heads innervated by different divisions of the parent nerve (tibial vs common fibular) and different actions (no hip extension).
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset; Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_from: the superior medial aspect of the ischial tuberosity
motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_to: the proximal aspect of the medial femoral epicondyle
motor_endplate_zones.method: cadaveric dissection to the proximal and distal limit points of the terminal intramuscular nerve endings
motor_endplate_zones.notes: The short head's arborisation sits distal to the long head's on the same line (39.7-72.9%), which matches its more distal origin on the linea aspera. Motor entry point at 56.2% (59.7% on the source's perpendicular axis), just proximal to the field. The short head answers to the common fibular division of the sciatic nerve and the long head to the tibial division, so separating them matters for a nerve block as well as for a needle.
motor_endplate_zones.source: An XC, Lee JH, Im S, Lee MS, Hwang K, Kim HW, Han SH, 'Anatomic localization of motor entry points and intramuscular nerve endings in the hamstring muscles', Surg Radiol Anat 32(6):529-537 (2010), doi:10.1007/s00276-009-0609-5 -- 50 cadaveric lower extremities. Retrieved via PubMed.

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse on the distal third of the posterior thigh, lateral portion.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Lies directly over the femoral cortex at this level.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Implicated in the excessive-knee-flexion gait pattern. The source states its arborization percentages along the femoral condyles (0%) to ischial tuberosity (100%) line, but those values sit in a list that full-text extraction dropped, so no motor_endplate_zones entry is recorded for this muscle. The reference line is known; the numbers are not, and are not inferred from the neighbouring hamstrings.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part III -- Proximal Lower Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(5):240 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17050240 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites
